sense.text:
“Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not honoured.” Israel’s princes hanged up, and the faces of the elders not honoured. That is our history, and it is why Strange Fruit hits different for us. Billie Holiday sang it in 1939: black bodies swinging in the southern breeze, blood on the leaves and blood at the root, strange fruit hanging from the poplar trees. It is a tearjerker, because it describes our struggles and hardships in the South, the way our people’s bodies were swinging from trees.

Most of our people could care less; they say slavery was a long time ago and they are getting the bag now. But students of the word of God, who understand Deuteronomy 28 and Leviticus 26, understand this historically: our princes hanged up, the faces of our elders not honoured.

And look who wrote that song. Strange Fruit was first a poem, written by a Jewish communist teacher from the Bronx, Abel Meeropol, moved by a 1930 photo of the lynching of two black men in Indiana. Yet the tiny hats, the Amalekites, were some of the chiefest slave owners and traffickers: they owned the slave ships’ insurance, the plantations, the newspapers and the history books, and there were Confederate Jews fighting to keep slavery in place. They used Strange Fruit, the way they co-wrote and marched in the civil rights movement, to catapult that movement for their own benefit. It was not to help so-called black people. Get that thought out of your mind. Regular Esau is not excluded from this either.

That is why we must constantly remind our people, who stray back into the Christian mindset, into forgetfulness, into unwarranted forgiveness, not to mention the bootlicking cool negro: like the court officer stroking the hair of the murderer Amber Guyger in the Botham Jean case, and the judge handing her a Bible. Whatever we watch or hear, we filter it through the scriptures.

“Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon, sit on the ground: there is no throne, O daughter of the Chaldeans: for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.” The virgin daughter of Babylon is Edom, the so-called white man. She is told to come down off her throne and sit in the dust.

This is the very one some of our people still revere: when they say Jesus, their mind goes straight to a white man that looks like Charles Manson. A news reporter went on national television and said Jesus was a white man, and said it with conviction, as if she had the authority, because she knew our people would just go along with whatever white folks say. The sister Crystal Valentine answered her: how can she say Jesus was a white man when he died the blackest way possible? That goes with Bishop’s class from over ten years ago, showing in the scriptures how Christ died a black man’s death, his beard plucked out and abused for the nation of Israel. Things like Strange Fruit and that poem are supposed to stir something up in us, and then we filter them through the scriptures.

“I was wroth with my people, I have polluted mine inheritance, and given them into thine hand: thou didst shew them no mercy.” God was angry with us and gave us into the hand of Edom, and Edom showed us no mercy.

They showed no mercy in Babylon of old, and the Lord goes back and forth between Babylon of old and Babylon the great, the daughter of Babylon, using one as a reference point for the other. So we go back and forth in time too: the 1930s, slavery, and then Derek Chauvin’s knee on George Floyd’s neck. Did he show any mercy? None.

When Eric Garner said he couldn’t breathe, the unmerciful Edomites made shirts that said I can breathe, while Edomite officers were using illegal choke holds and would not let go even when our brothers and sisters were in cuffs. An officer put his knee on the head of a dying Eric Harris and told him, F your breath. The article said it is hard for black Americans to catch our breath these days, as though before these days we could catch it. And it said those who police us can breathe quite easily. It is not just the police; it is at the hands of white folks. They are telling you on those shirts that they are the ones who police us. The Karens police us: show me your gate pass, show me your key card. The devils that killed Ahmaud Arbery were not police officers but a father and son vigilante group.

And it is speeding up. It used to be Trayvon Martin, then some time would go by, then Mike Brown. Now every time you turn on the TV it is some brother hung somewhere, drowned somewhere, or the alleged friends come back without that one person. Look how much the Lord is doing and allowing in these last days.

precepts.why:
For those who are new and do not know who the daughter of Babylon is: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” Then in the same breath, “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. The children of Edom are the daughter of Babylon, and she is set for destruction.

“Happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.” They are going to get double for what they have done to us. So when Isaiah 47 calls the virgin daughter of Babylon down into the dust, it is speaking of Edom, the so-called white man.

sense.text:
Jeremiah wrote this during the Babylonian captivity, Babylon of old. Let’s see if anything has changed. “As for us, our eyes as yet failed for our vain help: in our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save us.”

We are still watching for a nation that could not save us. We still trust that deliverance is going to come from the same people that had us on plantations, on ships, in the hot box, that gave us Derby’s dose and sicked their wild dogs on us. After all of those atrocities we still look to them, and to their descendants, to save us.

“They hunt our steps, that we cannot go in our streets”. The article about Eric Harris said the same thing: the inhumanity is not an aberration, it looks too much like these men being hunted. The police stalked Harris down like an animal. So is there any difference between Babylon of old and Babylon the great, the virgin daughter of Babylon, today? It is the exact same thing.

The Bible is very descriptive: we are trusting in the hunters. Sonya Massey called them for assistance, and the hunter threatened to shoot her in her face, and did exactly what he said he would do. Everyone who watched it knew she was no threat to this devil, but he deemed her a threat, being the merciless people they are created to be.

In 100 Years of Lynching, Ralph Ginzburg, an Edomite, documented over 5,000 lynchings in America over a hundred-year span. He shows the shiftless, propertyless younger group, without real jobs or responsibility, were the raw material for a lynching mob. The average age of the mob was 18 to 25, with older men frequently leading the group or making suggestions. The movies love to show old white men, but the foot soldiers at the forefront were the young ones, and some in the pictures were much younger than 18, like the children celebrating as they raided a black family’s house after the family was forced out in the 1919 Chicago race riots.

A teenager of 16 in 1935 would be 91 today. Some of those lynch mobs are still alive, being helped to their seats at the doctor’s office. And even if they are gone, they had upwards of 75 years to teach their sons, who are the judge over the courthouse now, the principal of the school, the doctor. You don’t think his daddy told him how they ran black folks out of their cities and burned their houses, and that is how they got their wealth?

“Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.” As iron rusts and gets older, so does his wickedness: it may change appearance, it got a little wear and tear, but it is the same iron and it is still there. The Karen mentality did not start with Trump in 2016; their mamas and daddies taught them: don’t trust these black folks, none of them are good. Anybody who thinks racism started because Trump went into office in 2016 is stupid; something is wrong with you. Nobody is saying push them down the stairs, but be mindful: never trust thine enemy, not even when he gets old.

Nolan Wells was 18, and his friends were all 18, the same age as the lynch mobs. Put up the picture of the lynch mob of today. “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” Black bodies swinging in the southern breeze: there is no new thing. Still a black body, still a southern breeze, in Mississippi. The end result is still the same.

The book says the cruelty of mobs has long furnished the students of crowd psychology with their best laboratory material. Their wickedness is studied the way serial killers are studied, because history says they are serial killers; yet today our people say, I don’t see color. And the cry heard from many throats at a lynching was, Let him die slowly; anything to prolong the agony. Is that not what the officer meant with his knee on Eric Harris’s head, F your breath? George Floyd died a slow, agonizing death, and Derek Chauvin was the leader of the lynch mob, telling the younger ones what to do. They have not changed.

“Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man; Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” They imagine mischiefs: let him die slowly. They imagined how to burn cities and towns down. At Sherman, Texas in 1930 the mob destroyed the Grayson County courthouse and burned the entire negro business section, and to stop the firemen they cut the hoses into little pieces. They threatened the law: give him to us or we burn down the station house. Violent, violent people.

They act so civil today, and make videos showing us as monkeys and say the degeneracy belongs to our people, while our people have forgotten the degeneracy of their oppressor. Their own history says it: an 1899 editorial said the annals of the savage will be searched in vain for anything worse than the exhibition given by the white civilization of the state of Georgia, and that no company of human beings ever showed greater joy in such a spectacle, rushing to secure pieces of the burned flesh and charred bones as mementos. Search every archive and every archaeological find and you won’t dig up anybody more wicked than the white man. When we say it, we are the bad guys, so we read it out of the Bible and out of their history books.

They try to demonize us with lower IQs and cranial this and that. Have you looked at West Virginia? The hills have eyes is a real place. They act as though they are the beacon of civilization and righteousness, but we are history buffs: we know what they really are, the cavemen from the Caucasus mountains. That is how much we pissed our God off, that these people are over us. Look at these damn inbreds. And the old record calls them what they are: whites are called demons.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent; adders’ poison is under their lips.” “Preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings. The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me.”

Seventy years after Money, Mississippi in 1955, to the date, Nolan Wells, the only black person on a boat of white kids, is found dead back in Mississippi. Bishop said as soon as he heard it, there was no wondering: they killed him. And the father said they raised their son not to see color. That is it right there.

precepts.why:
Who is the evil man and the violent man? “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

The border of wickedness. Above it the Lord said he hated Esau, and here it is not just Esau the man; it is a people, the people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever. That is the violent man of Psalms 140, the one history says nobody has ever outdone in wickedness.

sense.text:
We all want the kingdom: not pie in the sky, but dominion on the planet. “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” Through much tribulation: what we suffered in the time of Jim Crow, and it is coming back around.

Weeks ago on the same podcast Bishop said there will be more young men slain in the streets, and Nolan Wells happened after he said it. They understood there is a prophet among us. Our people have to be constantly reminded, because the Christian mindset takes us over. Even in 1933, while black bodies were still swinging, the New York Herald Tribune said mob violence was disappearing from the American way of life, and our people believed it. Is mob violence gone? No. Many of those police officers and judicial officials were the mob themselves, KKK members, the older men guiding it, handing our brothers over. Just as Bishop said, there is going to be more, and the Lord is going to ramp it up.

“And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest”. Among these nations we have found no ease, so the mindset that mob violence is disappearing is a lie. We should never be at ease. The scriptures tell us to be vigilant and watchful; never let your guard down. This is war: you are the only black person in a pool at a whole event, or at an all-white music festival, and they find you hanging.

We have to believe what God says. Your tax bracket may have changed and you may live comfortably around them, but God says you will find no ease. Brothers and sisters in million-dollar condos still get questioned by their neighbors about how they could afford it. And don’t feel comfortable around an Edomite baby: like Anthony Anderson taking the stairs rather than ride the elevator with a lost little white girl, because all she has to do is cry and you are thrown under the jail.

“But the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”: sorrow of mind that never ends. These curses are upon us. We have no ease.

precepts.why: Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28 run parallel. “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts”: the same trembling heart that Deuteronomy 28 says we will have among these nations, where we find no ease.

sense.text: “His children shall seek to please the poor, and his hands shall restore their goods.” His hands shall restore all the goods, because they will be servants.
“His bones are full of the sin of his youth, which shall lie down with him in the dust.” Since the time of Cain, Esau has never paid for his crimes. Not ever.

“Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth, though he hide it under his tongue; Though he spare it, and forsake it not; but keep it still within his mouth”. That goes right back to Ecclesiasticus 12:10: his wickedness rusts like iron, but it is still there, kept within his mouth.

The history book says lynching, as a typical American way of dispensing with the process of law, has always been with us: as American as apple pie, or biblically, Babylon. It says since the Civil War lynchings have markedly declined, but outbreaks of mob violence continue to be frequent. The same way they call slavery by another name, they call lynching by another name: no foul play, suicide, a missing person. It is not a public spectacle anymore, with the whole town gathered like at a ballgame to watch the body hang and burn; now only a chosen few are there. Medical examiners take out the throat and the internal organs, as with Kendrick Johnson, because they would show the trauma. The records only began in 1889, but before that they kept records in our teeth, our skin and our burned bones, handed down as mementos from generation to generation.

Donte Martin, a 19-year-old football player, went to an 18th birthday party at the isolated home of a known white supremacist in Fredericktown, Missouri, uncomfortable from the moment he got there. His right hand was in a thick cast and his right arm in a sling, yet he was found in the attic shot in the left temple, and the police ruled that he took his own life. He was embalmed before a second autopsy could be done. Nobody heard the gunshot. It was a modern-day lynching, and everyone at that party knew whose house it was and agreed with it. One organization found at least 70 suspected modern-day lynchings in seven southern states since 2000, bodies hanging with their feet on the ground, ruled suicide. That white supremacist was taught by his daddy, who was probably in the pictures we saw. Their wickedness has not changed; it is still within them. Search high and low and you won’t find anyone more wicked than the white man.

At least back in the day they had to hunt our brothers down and catch them. Now our people go to the slaughter themselves, like the sister in that picture who went to her own modern-day lynching, because it gives us some sense of accomplishment, of access to the kingdom, as though we can’t imagine the kingdom of heaven without these folks. Start wrapping your mind around them being in chains.

And they always justify it: if he was drinking, if he was on drugs, if a child had a toy gun. When George Zimmerman murdered Trayvon Martin, the news plastered a picture of Trayvon with a blunt, to say subconsciously that he deserved to die. They demonize the victims.

Brandon Tatum went down to Ocean Springs, Mississippi to discredit Nolan Wells and interview one of those involved, but the call to the boat towing company was recorded before the dispatcher picked up, and you hear them in the background: Is he dead? Nolan, don’t die. And the media acts shocked. Our entertainers are shocked because they have been given the impression that they have come a long way, while a white supremacist just walked into the Today studio past all the white people looking for Al Roker, yelling racial slurs. That was two weeks ago, and you think the lynching is done? Y’all are fast asleep. Wake your simple behind up. There is going to be more of this, because our people are still shocked by it.

“And they shall scoff at the kings, and the princes shall be a scorn unto them: they shall deride every strong hold; for they shall heap dust, and take it.” Edom scoffed at the kings: all of the caciques that were here, all of us that were in princely and kingly status, they mocked and slaughtered. They break down every stronghold.

“Then shall his mind change”. All of a sudden he doesn’t lynch as much anymore, because he is making money. He uses Jay-Z as the front to get the Barclays stadium built in downtown Brooklyn and push thousands of brothers and sisters out, and nobody makes an uproar. Al Sharpton is a puppet sent to calm the negroes down before they burn down the neighborhoods. Seneca Village, the 1919 Chicago pictures: nothing we see is new. They always have one of ours at the forefront to quench and quell our people. Brandon Tatum went all the way down to Mississippi to talk to the white man; he cried for Charlie Kirk and won’t shed a single tear for his people.

“And he shall pass over, and offend”: he will return to his original state and show fully that he is the same murderous people. They have never changed; they just put on nicer suits. “Imputing this his power unto his god”: his god is Satan, and he kills the children of Israel as a lynching, a sacrifice, unto his god.

The tip hotline set up in the Nolan Wells case turned out to be the number of a judge who is the mother of one of the alleged criminals. There is no new thing under the sun: the same police officers and judges that used to give black men and women over to the lynch mob are doing the same thing now. When will we learn?

“If thou seest the oppression of the poor”: you may say they live in nice houses and drive nice cars, they are not poor, but the oppression of the poor does not necessarily mean financially poor.

“And violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province”. There has always been a violent perverting of judgment, since they started documenting lynchings. Those coroner reports and medical examiners are violent perversions of justice, because someone should be serving time for those hangings and drownings, and people are getting off scot-free. A province is a regional administrative division inside a country, like a state, a county or a district: Ocean Springs, in its county, in the state of Mississippi.

“Marvel not at the matter”: don’t be shocked. They are perverting judgment and perverting evidence, and God says don’t be shocked by that. “For he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.” God is paying attention and keeping a watchful eye. We might miss things; God misses nothing. He sees every hiding of evidence, every perverting of judgment, and who is on the payroll. One of the fathers just offered a $50,000 reward to find the person that did it, when it was his own son.

precepts.why: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor of his people: there is a poor that is dealing with the spirit, not necessarily the finances. So the oppression of the poor in Ecclesiastes 5:8 is the oppression of the Lord’s people, whatever house they live in.

sense.text:
“So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter”.

“And on the side of their oppressors there was power”. It does not say on the side of the police force, or the judges, or the medical examiner; it says on the side of their oppressors. That is why Karen is so quick to say she will call the police: she knows there is power on her side. Back in the day they called Billy Bob and the lynch mob was on its way. It is no different today. “But they had no comforter.”

“Thus saith the Lord; Such as are for death, to death; and such as are for the sword, to the sword; and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for the captivity, to the captivity.” The Lord showed Jeremiah that some of our people are just for death. Jeremiah is the weeping prophet; he wept over the hurt of the daughter of Zion and the atrocities done in Babylon of old, the same way many of us feel in Babylon the great.

So why does this keep happening to our people? Everybody should answer with one consent: because we transgressed against the Lord our God.

“Their widows are increased to me above the sand of the seas”. For there to be widows, the men have to be killed. Esaw Snipes Garner, the widow of Eric Garner, died at 58. The NYPD choked him out, allegedly for selling loose cigarettes, and left her a weeping widow with their children. She is one of those widows.

“I have brought upon them against the mother of the young men a spoiler at noonday: I have caused him to fall upon it suddenly, and terrors upon the city.” God brought a spoiler against the mother of the young men. Isn’t Nolan Wells’ mother the mother of a young man? We have to understand who we are transgressing against: he is the king of terrors.

“She that hath borne seven languisheth”. Such as are for death, to death: these things must happen to the children of Israel, so that, as all these evils pronounced against us come to pass, Israel begins to ask, what is our transgression, what is our sin? You think there are a lot of young men slain now? As our people get worse and worse, the Lord has to turn up the fire even more.

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, when thou shalt shew this people all these words, and they shall say unto thee, Wherefore hath the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us?” Leadership has been saying there will be another Trayvon Martin, another Mike Brown, another Sandra Bland, and our people ask, why is all this evil happening to us? We just read why: some are for death to death, some for the sword, some for the famine.

“Or what is our iniquity? or what is our sin that we have committed against the Lord our God?” Our people have to get to that question. They ask why this keeps happening, but they have not yet found out or accepted that it is happening because of our sins. Our people knew this in the past, and we are bringing it back to the forefront of their minds. That is why the brothers in the highways and hedges, giving out a flyer or teaching one on one, teach with such fervency and urgency: we know there is going to be another Trayvon, another Nolan Wells.

“Then shalt thou say unto them, Because your fathers have forsaken me, saith the Lord, and have walked after other gods, and have served them, and have worshipped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my law”. Our forefathers transgressed the commandments of God.

“And ye have done worse than your fathers; for, behold, ye walk every one after the imagination of his evil heart”. The children today ask, what did we do that was so bad? The Lord says you are worse than your forefathers: your heart is wicked as hell. He made our forefathers walk in the wilderness forty years, and he says we are worse. So we warn our people: judgment is coming from God. Come out of that wickedness and amend your ways.

sense.text:
How can they continually pervert judgment, and how can we continually not get justice? “Whose possessors slay them, and hold themselves not guilty: and they that sell them say, Blessed be the Lord; for I am rich: and their own shepherds pity them not.”

Their own shepherds pity them not. The leaders set up over our people don’t pity them; they wait for the next one and make profit off of tragedy. Every time one of our brothers or sisters gets killed, they go on TV, file the civil case, the city or state pays, and they go cha-ching all the way to the bank.

“It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart.” Why is the Lord allowing brothers and sisters to be given death unto death? So that the living, us, will lay it to heart.

We are in the house of mourning now. As another Nolan Wells happens, another Sandra Bland, we lay it to heart and say, we really have transgressed against God; we really have pissed God off. And when you lay it to heart, those in the truth will no longer teach like a dead fish with dry eyes. You will be that lively stone in the street, teaching with fire to stir up the spirits of our people so they repent, and our people will begin to ask, what is our sin, how did we offend God so much that all of this has happened to us?

Here is some resolve as we lay these things to heart and search out our transgressions. “It came to pass also, that seven brethren with their mother were taken, and compelled by the king against the law to taste swine’s flesh, and were tormented with scourges and whips.” They were tormented by the same cruel, wicked, unforgiving people we have been looking at all class.

“But the mother was marvellous above all, and worthy of honourable memory: for when she saw her seven sons slain within the space of one day, she bare it with a good courage, because of the hope that she had in the Lord.”

As Jeremiah 15 said, some are for death unto death. That is out there now, and later it will be in here: they are going to want you to transgress the laws of God. Our people transgress willingly because they don’t know any better, hence our fervency to go out and wake them up to the fury of God. Where did they get, God is good all the time? He is good to Israel. Ask the Egyptians in the Red Sea, ask the inhabitants of the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. We have to endure the punishments, but he promises us mercy. He is not good to these nations, and if he hasn’t judged them yet, know for certain it is coming.

Antiochus “assured him with oaths, that he would make him both a rich and a happy man, if he would turn from the laws of his fathers; and that also he would take him for his friend, and trust him with affairs.” He tried to bribe him: riches, position, a political seat.

“But when the young man would in no case hearken unto him, the king called his mother, and exhorted her that she would counsel the young man to save his life.” They have done the same: they reached out to Nolan Wells’ mother and father, and to Trayvon Martin’s mother, and told her, if you don’t tell these people to calm down, they are going to be locked up. Tell them what needs to be said to save them. It is done out there, and it will be done in here, where they will force you to break the commandments of God.

“She promised him that she would counsel her son. But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn, spake in her country language on this manner; O my son, have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb”.

Sisters, that may be your son in that day; brothers, it may be your son. You don’t wake up one day thinking your son is never coming home. When that young man drove to that city for his friend’s party, he didn’t think he wasn’t going to make it home.

“For our brethren, who now have suffered a short pain, are dead under God’s covenant of everlasting life: but thou, through the judgment of God, shalt receive just punishment for thy pride.” We have to be so sound in that.

“But I, as my brethren, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers, beseeching God that he would speedily be merciful unto our nation; and that thou by torments and plagues mayest confess, that he alone is God”. That is what we ask: that the Lord be merciful unto our nation.
